_schema.site: title, eyebrow, run_header, conventions[], devices[] (order for per_device tables)
_schema.tabs[]: id (deep link #id), kind (paper | log | questions), label, title, subtitle, state (active | merged | archived), merged_into (tab id when merged), may_merge_into (tab id, shown as a notice), state_date, state_note, status {question, answer[], next[], updated}, sections[] {id, title, position (before_claims | after_claims), blocks[]}. Questions tab: open[] {question, context, source}, decided[] {question, decision, context, recorded, source}.
_schema.status items: string, or {text, source[], claim (claim id for a details link), queue_match (regex over queue labels; appends running/queued/done counts)}, or a block (object with type, e.g. batch_table) rendered inside the list
_schema.claims[]: id, tab, statement (one sentence), status (verified | in_progress | refuted | planned | invalid), headline {value, convention}, numbers[] {label, value, convention, source}, what[] (blocks), did[] (strings or blocks), result {text[], figures[] {batch, file, caption?}, tables[] (batch_table refs {batch, table, rows?, columns?} or inline tables), blocks[]}, caveats[], sources[], updated. A claim renders in its tab; when a tab is merged its claims render in merged_into.
_schema.blocks: string | {type: text|code|list|figure|table|batch_table|per_device|queue|timeline|nodes|facts, ...}. batch_table: {batch, table (heading prefix in tables.md), rows (first-cells prefixes joined by ' | '), columns (subset)}. per_device: {columns [{label, file, path with {device}}], caption, notes, mean_row}. queue: {match (regex)}.

site.title: Cryo-ML Research Results
site.run_header: T = 77 K · 18 measured SkyWater devices (8 nMOS, 10 pMOS), 11 I–V curves each · ngspice-41 (native arm64 build) · metric: paper RRMS (port of upstream rrmsCalc.py)
conventions: RRMS is the paper metric with the published-baseline curve inclusion frozen, scored on a fresh NGSpice re-simulation of the card, unless a claim says otherwise.
all-device = mean over the 18 devices. combined = mean of the nMOS (8) and pMOS (10) family means. The paper's headline 0.2038 (43 parameters) and 0.2284 (seven parameters) are all-device values.
raw = method output; + FD = after the uniform NGSpice finite-difference polish (`scripts/research/polish_cards.py`).
NGSpice calls per device: 'this run' counts the run's own simulations; 'cumulative' adds every bank and earlier round it used.

DEV = held-out simulated sets 0 and 1. TEST = the 18 real devices, simulated set 2 and the GF180/IHP test truths, run once per frozen method. Results on the real devices dated before 2026-10-16 18:00 were produced before this split was defined.

tabs.label: ICML 2027
tabs.title: ICML 2027: simulator-in-the-loop fitting
tabs.subtitle: Target: ICML 2027 main track. Fallback: NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks.

status.question: Does a trust-region fit that uses a neural surrogate as its model, corrected at each centre with the NGSpice value and Jacobian, reach direct-NGSpice accuracy with fewer NGSpice calls? Thesis under test: neural surrogates do not rank candidate cards in the order NGSpice ranks them, and inverse networks trained on simulations have large errors on measured devices (model misspecification).

answer.text: Same search with NGSpice in place of the surrogate, 43 parameters, round 1: all-device RRMS 0.2382 → 0.1125 (combined 0.2289 → 0.1053). The pipeline value is from its final selection rerun with the same surrogate and the rule that rejects candidates with failed included curves; 18 of 18 devices are valid. Before the fix the stored pipeline value was 0.2375, with 1 failed device (0.2395 over the 17 valid devices, 0.2920 penalized).

The round-1 43-parameter surrogate orders its own picks and the direct-fit cards opposite to NGSpice on 16 of 18 devices (surrogate 0.2474 vs 0.5074; NGSpice 0.2382 vs 0.1269, all-device), with the picks from the final selection rerun with failed-curve rejection. With the picks made before the fix the count was 17 of 18 (surrogate 0.2034; NGSpice 0.2375 stored, 1 device with a failed included curve).

Six surrogate architectures in the same search, 43 parameters, round 1: end-to-end all-device RRMS 0.2274–0.2549 vs 0.1125 with NGSpice in place of the surrogate; the lowest test loss (FNO) has the highest end-to-end RRMS. Diagnostic ablation on the measured devices, not used for method selection.

Learning curves, paper MLP / DeepONet / FNO at 10,732 → 85,853 training samples: test loss 4.8–5.4× lower; end-to-end all-device 0.2588 → 0.2348, 0.2581 → 0.2274, 0.2494 → 0.2549 (combined 0.2483 → 0.2248, 0.2477 → 0.2193, 0.2397 → 0.2448); NGSpice swap 0.1125. Diagnostic ablation.
Tandem inverse network (A), seven parameters: median device RRMS 0.0258 on held-out simulated devices, 0.6344 on measured devices.
Hybrid trust-region fit: DEV results at 500–5000 calls on 36 targets are in [dev-iter1](#claim-dev-iter1).

DEV iteration 1, pooled all-device RRMS at B500 / B5000: sketch_surrogate_k8 0.0313 / 0.0091; sketch_none_k8 0.0370 / 0.0021; anytime_sur_presearch_race 0.0287 / 0.0070; cmaes_trf 0.0565 / 0.0109. Targets are well-specified.

next.text: Misspecified DEV set from GF180/IHP tier c, then the same DEV comparison on it. Planned, not queued.
Hybrid trust-region fit on the round-1 and round-4 43-parameter boxes, with the surrogate and with no model (`--model none`), equal and successive-halving schedules.
GF180MCU and IHP SG13G2 truth sets and banks.
Surrogate architecture study on the round-1 43-parameter cache, with learning curves.

blocks.text: Each node is a method variant registered as a DEV arm in `out/research/dev/arms.json`. Method selection uses DEV only. DEV results for n1a, n1b and n1c: [dev-iter1](#claim-dev-iter1).

items.name: n1a · sketched Jacobians
items.method: At each trust-region centre, k = 8 directional NGSpice probes (Gauss-Newton step, top singular vectors of the transported prior, one Gaussian direction) plus secant and Broyden updates replace the 43-call FD Jacobian; a full FD Jacobian at the first centre, on refresh, and on prior mismatch. Control: the same code with no surrogate.

items.name: Hermite discrepancy correction
items.method: Multi-centre gradient-enhanced (Hermite) GP correction of the surrogate-NGSpice discrepancy, first-order consistent at the centre, using every NGSpice call including rejected trials. Proposed in iteration 1 and not selected for implementation.

items.name: n1c · CMA-ES call-trace baseline
items.method: CMA-ES (sigma0 0.3, popsize 15) then bounded TRF, and lq-CMA-ES, on the same oracle, bank start, objective and call accounting as the trust-region arms, with an exact trace of best RRMS against cumulative NGSpice calls.

items.name: n1b · anytime racing
items.method: Eight zero-call surrogate presearch starts, racing of trust-region runs by predicted reduction per NGSpice call, optimistic-bound drops, surrogate-proposed restarts.

items.label: DEV
items.value: Held-out simulated targets `set_0` and `set_1` (18 devices each, 36 targets) on the full round-1 43-parameter box, through `CRYOML_TARGET_OVERRIDE`. Method development and tuning read only DEV results.

items.label: TEST
items.value: The 18 real 77 K devices, simulated `set_2`, and the GF180/IHP test truths. Each frozen method runs on TEST once.

items.label: Primary metric
items.value: All-device mean paper RRMS (frozen inclusion), pooled over targets, at fixed cumulative NGSpice budgets per target (500, 1000, 2000, 5000). Every call counts, Jacobian probes and cliff retries included. The final card is scored by one fresh NGSpice simulation.

items.label: Secondary columns
items.value: Per-set all-device mean and combined, median, geometric mean, worst target, fraction below 1e-2 and 1e-3, area under the log10 RRMS-vs-calls curve, median calls to reach 0.05 and 0.01. No device is excluded.

items.label: References
items.value: Bank oracle: best sample of the pre-paid 10k bank per geometry (0 calls). Round-1 paper pipeline (its NGSpice validation calls), and pipeline + FD when present.

items.label: Paired tests
items.value: Arm minus reference per target: win/tie/loss, mean difference, 95% CI, Wilcoxon p. Each row reads one arm's own records; no minimum over arms is taken.

items.label: Method freeze.
items.note: Method development on DEV until then.

items.label: Submission.
items.note: The official ICML 2027 abstract and paper dates are not yet checked; in past years the abstract deadline was about one week before the paper deadline.

tabs.label: Exploration
tabs.title: Exploration phase: directions E1–E5 and iteration 2
tabs.subtitle: Each direction has a cheap probe and a pre-registered continue or kill rule, judged on REAL_DEV (12 measured devices) and simulated sets; REAL_TEST is not loaded. Directions to continue are chosen by about 2026-11-15.

status.question: Which directions beyond matching NGSpice show a measurable effect under their pre-registered rules: E1 learned compact-model correction, E2 misspecification-robust one-pass inference, E3 temperature generalization under misspecification, E4 held-out-curve prediction with uncertainty, E5 shared discrepancy?

answer.text: Iteration 10 in progress (2026-10-21): I10-1 room-temperature -> 4 K prediction on NIST g5v0d10v5 DEV, invalid run (V2: shifted cards fail BSIM4 parameter checks), stopped by rule; I10-2 class selection for the shared correction from training data, rule output stop (no selector meets C1 and C2). Iteration 9 in progress (2026-10-21): I9-1 NIST sky130 4 K regular-Vt DEV with the room-temperature card, P_a correct and P_b supported; I9-2 function-class ablation of the shared correction on 4 measured datasets: Q1 class-dependent, Q2 smallest matching class mlp16_s1, no class beats M_bias with fewer parameters. Iteration 8 in progress (2026-10-21): I8-1 NIST sky130 4 K DEV prospective test, P_a correct and P_b supported; I8-2 TEST predictions committed. Iteration 7 complete (2026-10-20): I7-1 training-set statistic S1_lodo for the transfer of the I3-2 correction, supported on 20 new simulated datasets (prospective); secondary S3 done (Spearman +0.985). I7-2 hierarchical per-device adjustment of the shared correction fitted on K = 2 / 4 curves, rule output inconclusive; GMR(c_hier, e_crossinterp) against the non-learned cross-curve control is above 1 on all four datasets. Iteration 6 (2026-10-20): I6-1 TU Delft 40 nm at 4.13 K and 295.0 K with a generic BSIM4 card, rule output refuted (R1 not met at 4.13 K); at 295.0 K the correction lowers the held-out RRMS. Iteration 5: I5-1 replication of I3-2 on IHP SG13G2 measured data, not replicated (300 K; also 233, 343, 398 K); matched by B1, B2. Iteration 4: I4-1 baselines for I3-2, rule output supported against baselines (development set); I4-2 interpretation analysis reported. Iteration 3: I3-1 KILL; I3-2 CONTINUE, follow-ups F1c (SPICE-native on ngspice-41) and F2 done. Iteration 2: I2-0 diagnosis done; I2-1 KILL; E3b CONTINUE on simulated tier M.

Iteration 12 (2026-10-21): I12-1 g v2 (d/s-symmetric smooth inputs, charge-free replica element, gm/gds penalty) on sky130 77 K, 18 devices: not deployable under the pre-registered rule. LODO all-device / combined v2 0.0774 / 0.0732 (v1 0.0732 / 0.0691, C0_refit 0.1043 / 0.0975); A1 GMR(v2, C0_refit) 0.787 [0.703, 0.884] passes, A2 GMR(v2, v1) 1.042 [0.967, 1.111] fails (margin 1.05). Q1 tight equivalence 0 violations; failed core checks: exchange asymmetry 1.35e-2, Q2 derivatives 2.31, Q2 capacitances 1.77e-3. Post hoc: capacitance and 4 of 5 derivative failures come from the reference run (BSIM4 A2 > 1 clamp applied only in the first analysis of a card-only process); nmos_L100_W100 derivative from the 1 MHz body-resistor term in the reference; exchange asymmetry from impact-ionization current in the sensed drain current.

I12-1 part B deployment checks: values vs thresholds

answer.text: Iteration 11 (2026-10-21): I11-1 M_bias as an ngspice-41 OSDI add-on on sky130 77 K (18 devices, M_full card + full-data g): not deployable under the pre-registered rule. Every element run converges; OSDI matches the Python model to 1.5e-6 above 10 nA, but the tight threshold fails at 1-3 nA (2.6e-5, 1e-14 A floor), the AC check fails at the Vgs = 0 abs() kink (6.4e-3), and gm turns negative on one curve (nmos_L100_W100). Restrictions: terminal asymmetry 0.117, drain displacement current x exp(g), 27/90 gds curves negative, ring-oscillator wall time 3.25x.

I11-2 (shared bias-only correction with a temperature input, held-out temperature; IHP SG13G2 DEV 18 DUTs at 233 / 300 / 343 / 398 K, TU Delft 40 nm DEV 45 devices at 4.13 / 295 K): invalid run, stopped by rule. V2 failed because the decide check compared the 398 K M_bias_near rows (343 K fold correction) with X300 rows (300 K fold correction); the 36 rows named in prereg.json are equal and the arm rows are correct. Descriptive: M_bias_T vs C0_refit 1.121 (interpolation) and 1.209 (extrapolation), vs M_bias_pool 1.008 / 1.008; TU Delft M_bias_X 0.978 / 1.460; 12/12 predictions 'no gain' correct. Recommendation: stop without re-registration.

items.value: A fresh in-box draw, plus every non-fitted misspecification parameter scaled by a log-uniform factor in [1/(1+w), 1+w] (w = 0.2 GF180, 0.05 IHP); extrinsic drain and source resistors outside the card (GF180 r ~ U(25, 100) ohm·µm / W; IHP r = k × RSW1, k ~ U(0.1, 0.4)); multiplicative Gaussian noise σ = 0.01.

items.label: c · strongly misspecified
items.value: A fresh in-box draw, plus non-fitted parameters with width 0.5; extrinsic resistors r = k × the card's own per-side series resistance, k ~ U(1, 2); self-heating-like heating, curve i at 27 C + ΔT_max · P_i / max P with ΔT_max ~ U(20, 40) K; bias-dependent noise σ(1 + |Vd|/VDD) with σ = 0.01; per-curve gain error 1 + N(0, 0.01).

what: Question: how much of the paper pipeline's error at 43 parameters comes from the surrogate rather than from the search procedure?

Paper pipeline (cold, round 1): a 10k-card Latin-hypercube bank per device in the round-1 box, simulated in NGSpice; a forward surrogate (parameters → I–V) trained on it from random initialization; 8 diverse bank starts; bounded TRF least squares on the surrogate with 2-point FD (max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4); NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the 4 starts and the fallback.

Swap control: the same `finite_difference_surrogate_extract` code with an NGSpice evaluator in place of the surrogate. Nothing else changes. Failed NGSpice points are penalized at curve RRMS 10. Round trip against the bank ≤5e-6 relative.
Box: cold round-1 box (vth0 ×3, the other six paper parameters ×100, the remaining screened parameters ×3, log-uniform). Devices: the 18 measured 77 K devices.

Dropped-curve bug: `metrics.device_rrms_new` averaged only the finite included curves, so a device whose included metric curve failed to simulate was stored with the mean of its surviving curves (upstream `rrmsCalc.py` gives NaN for that device), while the FD polish scored the same start with the penalized objective (RRMS 10 per failed curve). This gave the FD-start mismatches 0.2035 vs 1.1832 (pipeline 43 round 1, `nmos_L0p15_W1p6`, 1 of 10 included curves failed) and 0.0263 vs 9.0026 (pipeline 43 round 4, `nmos_L8_W1p6`, 9 of 10 failed). Fix: `cryoml.strict_score` marks such devices as failed and every report gives the failed-device count, the mean over valid devices and the penalized mean next to the stored value (commit 15d1f3e); `polish_cards.py` scores its start with `final_score` and records failed included curves (8302a9d); `metrics.device_rrms_new` now returns NaN for a device with a non-finite or missing included curve and the pipeline's NGSpice validation sorts such candidates last (a0e1e97). Result files written before the fix keep their stored values; `out/research/audit/failed_curves.json` recomputes the three values for 227 runs, 16 of which have a failed device.
Not a matched-budget comparison: the swap uses 19,854 NGSpice calls per device in this run against 10,009 for the pipeline (bank and validation). Matched-budget curves come from the DEV comparison.

what: Question: does a different or larger surrogate architecture, trained on the same data with the same recipe, change the end-to-end result of the pipeline's search on the measured devices?

Architectures (`src/cryoml/operators.py`): paper MLP (4 × 1024 hidden, 5.3M trainable parameters), wide MLP (6 × 2048, 25.3M), residual MLP (27.3M), large residual MLP (138.6M), DeepONet (branch residual MLP, trunk over the bias point, 25.8M) and an FNO conditioned along each curve's sweep axis (4.1M).

Fixed across architectures: the round-1 43-parameter cache (`out/cold_loop/full/round_1/cache`); the per-device train/validation/test split of the pipeline (seed 20260818, 85,853 training samples); the loss (standardized signed-log MSE + curve-normalized linear Huber); the recipe (AdamW, cosine schedule, early stopping on validation loss, at most 200 epochs, FNO at most 80); and the search (`fps.finite_difference_surrogate_extract`: 8 starts, TRF max_nfev 100, diff_step 0.02, regularization 1e-4, NGSpice validation of the top 4 endpoints, the first 4 starts and the published fallback).

Measured per architecture: test loss and curve NRMSE on held-out bank samples; surrogate-predicted and NGSpice RRMS of three reference card sets (the stored pipeline r1 picks, direct NGSpice cold, direct NGSpice seeded); and the end-to-end search on the 18 measured devices, each selected card re-simulated in NGSpice.

n1a, sketched Jacobians (`scripts/research/sketch_tr.py`): the trust-region loop of `hybrid_tr` with the 43-call FD Jacobian replaced at most centres by k directional NGSpice probes (Gauss-Newton step, top singular vectors of the transported prior, one Gaussian direction) plus secant and Broyden updates; a full FD Jacobian at the first centre, every 6 iterations and on prior mismatch; subproblem max_nfev 30. n1b, anytime racing (`scripts/research/anytime_tr.py`, `src/cryoml/racing.py`): `anytime_sur_presearch_equal` runs 8 zero-call surrogate TRF presearches from bank starts, validates them with 8 NGSpice calls, and splits the budget equally over the 2 best endpoints and 2 bank starts without restarts; `anytime_sur_presearch_race` uses the presearch starts, allocates calls by predicted reduction per NGSpice call, drops runs by an optimistic bound and restarts from surrogate-proposed points; `anytime_none_race` uses 4 bank starts, Gauss-Newton trust regions, the same racing and drops, and bank-start restarts, with no presearch.

n1c, CMA-ES call-trace baselines (`scripts/research/cmaes_trace.py`): `cmaes_trf` (CMA-ES with sigma0 0.3 for 60% of the budget, then bounded TRF with diff_step 1e-3 and regularization 1e-4) and `lq_cmaes` (lq-CMA-ES, 9 restarts), on the same oracle, bank start, objective and call accounting as the trust-region arms.

what: Question: when a device's 43-parameter card is fitted to a subset of its measured I-V curves, do an ensemble of near-optimal cards, a Gauss-Newton Laplace approximation, or a discrepancy model learned on other devices give calibrated predictive intervals and lower RRMS on the unmeasured curves than the single best-fit card?

what: Question: E1 stage 2 and I2-1 showed that a per-(family, curve tag) gain table T1 lowers the held-out RRMS after the card refit, while the E1 network M (inputs is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD, log10 L, log10 W, log10 |I_sim| L/W) does not reach T1. A curve tag is a fixed terminal bias, so T1 is a function of polarity and bias only. I3-2 tests whether a smooth network of polarity and bias only, with no geometry input and no simulated-current input, matches T1 and beats the refit without a correction.

items: Corrected current: I_corr(V) = I_sim(card; V) · exp(g(x)), x = (is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD), VDD = 1.85 V. The multiplication keeps the sign and zero crossings of I_sim.

g(x) = (1/5) Σ_{s=0..4} tanh(h_s(z)), z = standardized x (fold training mean and std; is_pmos kept 0/1); h_s = MLP 3-16-16-1 with tanh hidden units and a zero-initialized last layer (353 weights per member).

Training loss = (1/N_train) Σ_devices RRMS_dev(I_sim · exp(g), I_meas) + 1e-4 Σ ||W||², RRMS_dev = mean over the frozen-included curves of RMSE / mean |I_meas| on the trimmed points (paper metric). Adam lr 3e-3, 2000 full-batch steps, float64, seeds 0-4.

Held-out refit: minimize the residuals of I_bsim(card) · exp(g) against the held-out device's measured curves over the 43 card parameters (ngspice_fit.polish, trust-region least squares, max_nfev 400, 2 IRLS rounds, diff_step 0.01), starting from the device's direct43_r3_fd card; g frozen. Score: fresh NGSpice simulation of the best card times exp(g), strict paper RRMS with frozen inclusion.
Arms: C0_refit (control, same refit with g = 0); M_bias (primary); M_bias_geom (secondary, adds log10 L and log10 W: 5-16-16-1); T1_inloop (per-tag gains, not deployable, comparator).

Rule (pre-registered): CONTINUE only if R1 upper CI bound of R(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1 on REAL_DEV; R2 M_bias all-device <= T1_inloop + 0.005; R3 0 failed devices; R4 R(M_bias, C0_refit) <= 0.90 and 0 failed on GF180 or IHP tier c. STOP otherwise.

what: Question: does a simpler or physics-based change to the held-out card refit give the same held-out strict paper RRMS as the I3-2 correction M_bias (I = I_card · exp(g), g = tanh(MLP 3-16-16-1 of is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD), card refit with g in the loop)?

items: B1: base box plus extra card parameters (sky130 19, GF180 35, IHP 71) selected by an edge screen of the starting cards (response >= 1e-4 at a box edge), fitted jointly, no correction.

B2: equal extrinsic series resistors on drain and source in the netlist (box [0, 4 R_side / W]) and a factor exp(kappa |Vds I| / P_max) (kappa in [-0.5, 0.5]), fitted jointly with the base box, no learned term.
B3_d2 / B3_d3: shared g = tanh(polynomial of total degree 2 / 3 in standardized |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD), separate coefficients per polarity (12 / 20 coefficients), trained with the E1 loss.
B4: shared GP posterior mean of ln|I_meas / I_sim| on (is_pmos, |Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD), ARD squared-exponential kernel + white noise, type-II maximum likelihood, 2000 points per fold.
B5 (reference, not in the rule): M_bias-form ensemble trained on the held-out device's own record, refit with it in the loop, retrained on the refit card.

B1 and B2 are local refits from the same starting card as C0_refit; their max_nfev is scaled with the parameter count so that the TRF evaluations per IRLS round equal the base-box value of the same device.
Rule: X is beaten if the REAL_DEV CI upper bound of GMR(M_bias, X) < 1, or GMR(M_bias, X) < 0.95 on both GF180 and IHP tier c. 'Supported against baselines' if every X is beaten.

what: Question: does the 43-parameter card + shared bias-only correction (M_bias, I3-2 recipe, I = I_card x exp(g(is_pmos, |Vgs|/1.85, |Vds|/1.85))) work as a compact-model add-on in circuit simulation? The stored full-data Verilog-A (trained on all 18 sky130 77 K devices) is compiled with OpenVAF 23.5.0 and placed as an OSDI element around the BSIM4 instance (drain moved to an internal node; sense branch V(sense) <+ RS*I(sense), RS = 0) in the ngspice-41 OSDI build.

Pre-registered (in force from da03859): core checks Q1 tight equivalence <= 1e-5, 0 convergence messages, |I(Vds = 0)| <= 1e-12 A; Q2 AC derivative difference <= 1e-3 and 0 introduced gm sign changes in strong inversion; Q3 0 circuits failing only with the element. Restrictions: default-tolerance difference > 1e-3, terminal asymmetry > 1e-3, drain displacement current changed, introduced gds sign changes, wall-time ratio > 2. Outcome: not deployable / deployable with restrictions / deployable (simulator-level).
did: Card M_full: per device the 43-parameter card refit from direct43_r3_fd with the full-data g in the loop (max_nfev 400, irls 2), 171 s. Q1: 11,175-point grid per device at three tolerances, plus drain/source-exchanged instances. Q2: 600 op points per device with op + AC at 1 MHz (gate and drain excitation), 1 mV sweeps. Q3: inverter VTCs, 5-stage ring oscillators and 1:1 mirrors with 4 arms. Q4: median of 3 wall times. Total run 3.4 min, 4 workers. Post hoc diagnosis in diagnosis.json.
Report `scripts/research/plot_explore_i11_1.py` (batch 2026-10-21_i11_1) recomputes the decision from the stored summary values and checks them against q12.json.

text: Outcome (pre-registered rule): not deployable. Core failures: (1) tight-tolerance difference 2.6e-5 > 1e-5 at 1.0-2.6 nA, absolute differences <= 2.8e-14 A (gmin and bypass settings do not remove them); (2) AC derivative difference 6.4e-3 at Vgs = 0 on nmos_L100_W100, where abs() has a derivative jump and OSDI takes a one-sided derivative; elsewhere <= 7.3e-6; (3) gm becomes negative on nmos_L100_W100 at |Vds| 0.05 V, |Vgs| 1.757-1.85 V, where the card alone has positive gm.

Restrictions found: at default tolerance the difference is 1.9e-3 (reltol-level); the element is not source/drain symmetric because g uses the instance source terminal; it multiplies the whole drain-terminal current including displacement and junction currents (drain capacitive admittance scaled by exp(g)); 27 of 90 gds curves acquire negative values (mainly long pMOS; the measured average slopes on those curves are positive); the 5-stage ring oscillator runs 3.25x slower.

No circuit fails only because of the element. The M_full card itself (with or without g) and the C0_refit card stop the ro5_B transient (pmos_L2_W5 card, 'timestep too small'); the published card runs. Circuit differences between arms are small for the inverter (V_M within 1.3 mV of the card alone) and up to 2.3% for the pMOS mirror ratio.

Next actions (new pre-registration each): source/drain-symmetric g input; apply exp(g) to the channel current only (correction inside a Verilog-A BSIM4); train g with a penalty on negative gm / gds; smooth abs(); restate the equivalence check as relative plus absolute tolerance.

caveats: Simulator-level only: there is no measured circuit data, so Q3 shows consistency and convergence, not accuracy.
The tight threshold 1e-5 was set after a 2-device smoke (2.5e-6); on 18 devices the floor reached 2.6e-5.
The M_full RRMS is in-sample; the held-out (LODO) M_bias value is 0.0732.
Wall times were measured while another 6-worker job was running.

what: Question: when a held-out device is characterized by K = 2 or 4 of its curves, does a low-dimensional per-device adjustment of the shared bias-only correction, fitted with the card on those curves under a prior learned from the training devices, lower the strict paper RRMS on the device's other curves? In I3-2, I5-1 and I6-1 the in-sample per-device correction B5 was about 2x lower than every shared arm.

items: Model: I_corr = I_card x exp(g_d), g_d = g_shared + phi . delta_d, phi = (1, a, b, a^2, ab, b^2), a = 2|Vgs|/VDD - 1, b = 2|Vds|/VDD - 1. g_shared = the stored fold M_bias correction of I3-2 (sky130), I5-1 (IHP 300 K) or I6-1 (TU Delft), not retrained.

Prior per fold: delta_j of each training device fitted on its starting record with the card fixed; N(m, S), S = 0.5 Sigma_hat + 0.5 diag(Sigma_hat) + 1e-6 I; whitened z = Lc^-1 (delta - m). MAP objective on the K curves: mean curve RRMS + mu |z|^2. mu is selected per fold and K from {0, 1e-5, ..., 1, inf} on the training devices (card fixed, leave-one-out prior); mu = inf gives delta = m.

Draws: Id-Vg curves ordered by |Vd|, Id-Vd by |Vg|; K2a = top Id-Vg and top Id-Vd; K2b = lowest Id-Vg and middle Id-Vd; K4a = K2a + K2b; K4b = Id-Vg and Id-Vd at the 1/3 and 2/3 positions. Held-out set = every other included curve (at least 2).

Per split: start card (box center or training median, lower K-curve RRMS), base fit on the K curves, then each arm refits from the base card on the K curves (polish 400, irls 2): a_C0 (no correction), b_shared (g_shared), c_hier (joint card + z, primary), c_ml (mu = 0), d_scratch (from-scratch per-device MLP on the K curves), e_crossinterp (a's card + cross-curve residual). Score: fresh NGSpice simulation of the final card on all curves times exp(g), strict paper RRMS on the held-out curves.

Rule: C1 CI upper of GMR(c, b) < 1 on >= 3 of 4 datasets; C2 CI upper of GMR(c, a) < 1 on 4 of 4; C3 GMR(c, d) < 1 on 4 of 4 and CI upper < 1 on >= 3; C4 c failures <= 10% and >= 8 paired. Outcomes in order: invalid, supported_continue, delta_no_gain_stop (GMR(c, b) >= 0.98 on >= 2), sharing_no_gain (C1, C2, not C3), inconclusive.

text: Rule output 'inconclusive': C1 holds on 2 datasets (TU Delft 4.13 K and 295 K; IHP 300 K CI upper 1.024, sky130 point 0.992), C2 on 3 (IHP 300 K 1.025), C3 on 1 (sky130 0.912). The delta_no_gain_stop condition is met on 1 dataset (sky130), not on 2.

e_crossinterp, which uses no learning and no extra simulation, has the lowest held-out RRMS of all arms on TU Delft 4.13 K (GMR(e, a_C0) 0.585, 45/45) and 295 K (0.673); GMR(c_hier, e_crossinterp) is above 1 on all four datasets.

The learned prior is not better than the flat prior: GMR(c_hier, c_ml) 1.126 (sky130), 0.930 (IHP), 1.005 (TU Delft 4.13 K), 1.065 (295 K). On sky130 the empirical-Bayes selection chose mu = inf in 44/48 splits, so c_hier there applied the fold's mean delta to every device.

The order changes with K. At K = 2, c_hier is ahead of d_scratch on sky130 (0.897), TU Delft 4.13 K (0.851) and 295 K (0.984), and behind on IHP (1.148). At K = 4, d_scratch is ahead of c_hier on IHP (1.392), TU Delft 4.13 K (1.562) and 295 K (1.278), and behind on sky130 (0.959); at K = 4 the two lowest arms are d_scratch and e_crossinterp on IHP and both TU Delft datasets. GMR(c, b) is lower at K = 4 than at K = 2 on IHP and TU Delft.
The per-device term is small on the held-out points: median RMS of phi . delta for c_hier is 0.005-0.015 in ln I (0.5-1.5% in current), below the RMS of g_shared except on IHP.

The example-device figures (08-11) show measured points only: the arm I-V curves are not stored (results.json keeps RRMS, cards.json the cards, d_scratch's MLP is not stored) and were not re-simulated in this batch.

caveats: DEV devices of all four datasets were used by earlier directions; I7-2 results are development evidence. REAL_TEST and TEST were not loaded.
The prior and mu are estimated on training devices whose cards were fitted to all their curves (card fixed), while the held-out card is fitted on K curves (stated in the pre-registration).
The 4 draws per device are not independent; the per-device value is their geometric mean. TU Delft devices share geometry groups (cluster-bootstrap CIs in figure 02 are wider than the device CIs).
IHP: 3 of 18 DUTs have no K4 draw. sky130: one device failed in every arm; d_scratch and e_crossinterp also failed in one K4b split.

what: Question: can a statistic computed from the training devices of a fold alone predict whether the I3-2 shared bias-only correction M_bias lowers the held-out RRMS (y = ln GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) < 0) on a dataset?

items: S1_lodo: per training device, residual r = clip(ln(|I_target| / |I_sim|), -1, 1) of the starting card at included points, weight w = (|I_target| / den)^2 / (n points x n curves) (first-order M_bias loss); shared function m = weighted bin mean on a 12 x 12 grid of (|Vgs|/VDD, |Vds|/VDD) per polarity; S1_lodo = 1 - sum_d E_d(m without d) / sum_d E_d(0). Secondary: S1_pooled (m includes d), S2 (pairwise weighted cosine), S3 (inner leave-one-group-out post-hoc gain).

Step 2: 11 stored datasets (sky130 77 K, IHP measured 233/300/343/398 K, TU Delft 4.13/295 K, GF180 / IHP tiers b and c), 162 folds; OLS line y = a + b S1_lodo frozen in a dated amendment before any step-3 data.

Step 3: 20 new simulated datasets: GF180 (BSIM4, ngspice-41) and IHP (PSP103, ngspice-46), 2 replicates, lambda in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}; truth = tier-a card x exp(e_d) x (1 + 0.01 N(0,1)), e_d = 0.10 (sqrt(lambda) s_polarity + sqrt(1 - lambda) u_d), s and u_d random Fourier feature functions of the normalized bias. I3-2 / F2 pipeline unchanged; 16 leave-one-geometry-out folds per dataset.
Prediction: P1 Spearman(S1_lodo_D, y_D) <= -0.50; P2 frozen-rule sign correct in >= 15 of 20; supported if both, partially supported if one, not supported if neither.

text: Across the 20 new datasets S1_lodo and y have Spearman -0.970 (P1 holds) and the frozen rule gives the correct sign on 16 (P2 holds): verdict 'supported'. S1_pooled and S2 give -0.974 and -0.979.
The 4 errors are datasets with S1_lodo between -0.103 and +0.006 (below the zero crossing 0.0157) and a small observed gain (y -0.131 to -0.037).

The prospective OLS slope is -1.419 against the frozen slope -0.485 (rule MAE 0.357): on the simulated data the gain grows with S1_lodo about 3 times faster than on the stored datasets. The rule predicts the sign, not the magnitude.

Within a dataset the fold-level relation has the opposite sign (positive in 20/20 new datasets, 0.28 to 0.96): a fold whose training set has a higher S1_lodo has a smaller gain on its held-out device.

S3 (secondary) ranks the datasets with Spearman +0.985 (20 new) and +0.927 (11 stored), and its sign matches the sign of y on 19/20 and 9/11. TU Delft 4.13 K, the largest residual of the frozen S1_lodo rule (+0.174), lies near the S3 lines (+0.058 stored-data OLS, +0.006 new-data OLS). Within a dataset S3 also reverses sign (negative in 20/20 new datasets). S3 costs 2409 s + 3442 s of queue time; S1_lodo needs no training.

caveats: The synthetic error of step 3 is of exactly the shared-plus-device form that S1_lodo measures, on the same normalized-bias inputs as M_bias (pre-registration step3_prospective.error_functions). The prospective test checks the statistic under its own model.

The evidence outside that model is the 11 retrospective datasets (7 measured, 4 simulated tiers), whose outcomes were known when S1_lodo was defined and the rule was fitted; the IHP measured temperatures share devices, as do the TU Delft temperatures.
The within-lambda and residual analyses are post hoc; each lambda level holds 4 datasets.

S3 (secondary) does not enter P1, P2 or the frozen rule; it has no frozen rule, and its sign agreement is reported, not pre-registered. S3 on the stored datasets was computed with their outcomes already known.

The stock-card RRMS is 0.66-23.1 per device and temperature; the starting cards come from a 43-parameter fit with a box of |v|/10..10|v|.

B1 returned the starting card unchanged for 16/45 devices at 4.13 K and 13/45 at 295.0 K and is above C0_refit on 34/45 and 33/45 devices.
The sweeps start near or above threshold (Vg from 0.45 / 0.30 V nMOS, -0.60 / -0.40 V pMOS); there is no deep-subthreshold data.
Training pools hold 31-43 devices of both polarities (sky130 I3-2: 11 devices; IHP I5-1: 7 or 9 within class).
The M_bias I-V curves are ngspice-41 currents of the refit card multiplied by exp(g) in Python, not SPICE-native simulations of the correction.

Split DEV 18 / TEST 10 (seed 20261020); TEST not loaded.
Cards: stock PSP103 PDK card; 12-parameter pdk2 IHP wide set fitted from the stock card (starting card); every held-out arm refits from the starting card (max_nfev 400, irls 2).

Arms: C0_refit (control), M_bias (I3-2 recipe unchanged; training within class, VDD 1.2 V LV / 3.3 V HV), T1_inloop, B1 (wider PSP set), B2 (extrinsic resistance + heating factor), B3_d3 (polynomial g), B5 (in-sample reference), X300 (300 K correction applied at 233/343/398 K).
Rule at 300 K: R1 CI upper of GMR(M_bias, C0_refit) < 1; R2 M_bias mean <= T1_inloop mean + 0.005; R3 0 failed -> 'replicated'. Baselines B1, B2, B3_d3 beaten if CI upper of GMR(M_bias, X) < 1.

text: At 300 K M_bias is above C0_refit (0.0203 vs 0.0191) and below it on 9 of 18 DUTs; R1 fails. R2 and R3 hold. Rule output: not replicated. The same holds at 233, 343 and 398 K.
B1 and B2 are below C0_refit at every temperature (GMR 0.695-0.809 and 0.886-0.946) and below M_bias at 300 K (GMR(M_bias, B1) 1.567, GMR(M_bias, B2) 1.284). Baseline rule output: matched by B1, B2.
The C0_refit level on IHP 300 K (0.0191) is 5.6 times lower than on sky130 77 K REAL_DEV (0.1072). M_bias closes -0.090 of the C0_refit -> B5 gap on the means (sky130: 0.403).

I-V figures 11-14 combine the stored stock-card figure (measured points and stock card) with the stored refit figure (measured points, C0_refit card, M_bias refit card x exp(g)); hv_pmos_W10_L0p35 has no stored stock-card figure. B1 and B2 cards are not plotted.

caveats: DEV results are development evidence; the rule, budgets, box and arms were fixed after the stock-card RRMS was seen and before any fit. TEST (10 DUTs) is not loaded.

The IHP runs use NGSpice-46 + psp103.osdi (OpenVAF-Reloaded); the sky130 runs use ngspice-41. The IHP RRMS freezes inclusion from the measured current, the sky130 RRMS from the published-card baseline.
The IHP refit has 12 PSP parameters from a starting card fitted to the same DUT; the sky130 refit has 43 BSIM4 parameters. The C0_refit levels differ by a factor of 5.6.
Training pools are within class: 9 LV or 7 HV training DUTs per fold (sky130: 11).

The M_bias I-V curves are NGSpice-46 currents of the refit card multiplied by exp(g) in Python, not SPICE-native simulations of the correction. The stored refit I-V figures do not contain the stock-card curve; it is taken from separate stored figures for 3 of the 4 DUTs.

what: Question: does a hybrid temperature law x(T) = par3_d(T) + sigma_h NN(geometry, par3 anchor residuals, T), with the per-device par3 law fitted on the O4 anchors (77/150/225/300 K) and a network shared across a densely characterised simulated population, predict the seven-parameter card at 110/190/260 K with lower NGSpice RRMS than par3 and lrn_mean when the truth law is outside the par3 family (tiers M and H), and not worse than par3 by more than a margin when the truth is inside it (tier W)?

The design addresses three E3b findings: lrn did not differ from lrn_mean on tier M; lrn lost to par3 on tier W; tier M and W were seen before the design. Tier H (piecewise-linear law with a kink plus a 5 K freeze-out step on vth0 and u0) was written in the pre-registration and not simulated before the decision run.

items: hyb network output initialised to 0, output penalty 0.01 mean(NN^2), early stopping that can return the zero-correction state; 5 members, each keeps the better of input sets geo_t and geo_t_res (addendum, before any NGSpice run of the new arms).
hyb_mean = par3 + population-mean residual per device type and temperature (no network).

CONTINUE: M1 GMR(hyb, par3) <= 0.80 with CI upper < 1; M2 CI upper of GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1; M3 GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1; W1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on W <= 1.25; H1 CI upper of GMR(hyb, par3) on H < 1; H2 GMR(hyb, lrn_mean) < 1 and GMR(hyb, pt_interp) < 1 on H; F failed cells <= 10%.
KILL: not CONTINUE and any of GMR(hyb, par3) >= 0.95 (M), >= 1.50 (W), >= 1.00 (H). INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.

text: Conditions: M1 met (0.741 [0.610, 0.901]); M2 not met (CI upper 1.312); M3 met (0.885); W1 not met (CI upper 2.132); H1 not met (CI upper 1.422); H2 not met (1.306, 1.763); F met. KILL conditions hit on W (1.739 >= 1.50) and H (1.224 >= 1.00). Rule output KILL.

hyb applies the correction at the anchor temperatures as well; its anchor-temperature mean RRMS is 0.213 (M), 0.089 (W) and 0.178 (H), against 0.171, 0.038 and 0.081 for par3 and 0.015, 0.012 and 0.013 for lrn, which returns the anchor fits at the anchors.

On tier H, lrn (the E3b method) has GMR 0.752 [0.640, 0.886] vs par3 and 0.802 [0.697, 0.919] vs lrn_mean, and 1.083 [1.010, 1.164] vs pt_interp (lower on 15/36). Its E3-rule output on tier H is INCONCLUSIVE (R_O4 0.145 < 0.25; reduction vs pt_interp 0.049 < 0.10). On tier W lrn has GMR 2.603 vs par3 (E3-rule output INCONCLUSIVE, as in E3b).
Scaling (tier M): from 36 to 144 training devices the lrn held-out mean goes 0.2644 -> 0.2778 -> 0.2468 and hyb 0.3333 -> 0.3086 -> 0.3102.

No hyb ensemble member returned the zero-correction state (best steps M 75-2999, W 25-375, H 50-125). Existing arms reproduce the E3b full runs on tiers M and W (max |difference| 0; O2 par3_pop 1.7e-7 on M).

caveats: Simulated devices only; training and test devices of each tier come from the same generator (no train-on-one-law, test-on-another condition).
Tier H was written by the same authors as tiers M and W, after seeing E3b; it is new to the hybrid design but not independent of the authors' assumptions about temperature laws.
The hyb inputs and output penalty were changed by the addendum after a synthetic unit test and before any NGSpice run of the new arms.
hyb has no gating at the anchor temperatures (pre-registered); its anchor-temperature error enters the card at all temperatures.
